exposure: Immune cell populations (CD14+, CD4+, CD8+ cells)
cohort: The study included patients with uncomplicated pregnancies (controls) and patients diagnosed with postpartum preeclampsia.
finding: Placental CD163+ cells and 1st trimester blood pressures can serve as valuable non-invasive and predictive biomarkers of PPPE, with observed maternal immune changes at diagnosis suggesting a dampened response with an exhausted phenotype.
followup_time: Up to 6 weeks postpartum (for PPPE development); blood samples collected at diagnosis, which occurred between 48 hours and 25 days postpartum (mean 7.4 days).
cross-section timing: Blood samples were collected at the time of PPPE diagnosis (48h-25 days postpartum) for cases, and 24 hours after delivery for controls.
